public_rationale: CNBC reported on 20 February 2026 that OpenAI generated $13.1 billion in revenue during calendar 2025 [e1]. This materially exceeds the scenario's assumed revenue of approximately $11.6 billion, which the contract treats as an amount, not a minimum [e1]. The revenue condition therefore did not hold, leaving the conditional spending and loss forecast untested by the reported result [e1].
limitations: The report does not establish whether 2025 spending per dollar of revenue matched the assumed $2.25 on a comparable accounting basis [e1].
The reported $8 billion burn figure does not establish comparable total spending or spending-minus-revenue loss [e1].
CNBC cites unnamed sources and does not provide the underlying financial records [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If OpenAI burns at its 2024 rate and hits $11.6B revenue, it will burn over $26 billion in 2025 for a loss of about $14.4 billion.
conditions: OpenAI burns at 2024 rate of $2.25 per $1 revenue

statement.excerpt: The New York Times reports that OpenAI projects it'll make $11.6 billion in 2025, and assuming that OpenAI burns at the same rate it did in 2024 — spending $2.25 to make $1 — OpenAI is on course to burn over $26 billion in 2025 for a loss of $14.4 billion.

from_speaker: assuming that OpenAI burns at the same rate it did in 2024
our_interpretation: Assess the conditional scenario, rather than treating its spending and loss figures as unconditional predictions.
The conditions are annual revenue of approximately $11.6 billion and spending of approximately $2.25 per dollar of revenue.
Treat $11.6 billion as the assumed revenue level, rather than a minimum threshold.
In this passage, burn means total spending. Loss means spending minus revenue; the passage does not establish a formal net-income accounting definition.
Allow ordinary rounding in the approximate loss figure.
criteria.support_condition: Both assumptions hold on a comparable accounting basis, and realized calendar-2025 spending exceeds $26 billion with an approximately $14.4 billion spending-minus-revenue loss.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Both assumptions hold, but comparable realized spending or loss materially conflicts with the forecast.
